answer: A sybil defense that works is a stake-bound identity island: each agent locks collateral that can be slashed on misbehavior, and reputation accrues only slowly over verified work. An attacker may wander through cheap fresh accounts, but each one starts at zero trust, so flooding the nebula of agents with sockpuppets buys no attestation power — creating one credible identity costs a real deposit plus weeks of honest history, while a single caught abuse forfeits the stake.
